title: Setup
text:
To use quarto I would suggest using VScode (You can “Disable Ai Features” in the settings).
To install Quarto see The Quarto Get Started page.


For this site you will also want to follow the below install instruction.


R in Visual Studio Code



Code Spell Checker: Useful for spell checking normal words
When using this click on a misspelt word (signified by squiggly underlining) and press “ctrl+.” to get a dropdown of suggestions
To change to GB spelling:

Go to “Extension” on VScode (On far left, icon is three squares and a diamond)
Click on the gear icon for Code Spell Checker
Click on “Settings”
Change “C Spell: Language” to “en-GB”





You can create a quarto project in 2 different way, a quarto command or copying a template.


In the command palette in VScode (the text bar at the top middle) type in the following:
>Quarto: Create Project
Further instructions are here: Quarto Website Quick Start



Optionally, you can copy a template or other project from github and edit it.
If you already have the files you can then copy and paste to a new directory (ensure you don’t copy over any git files/directories if you do this).
To download all the files of a gihub repo:

Navigate to the page via a browser (e.g. https://github.com/m-gemmell/Quarto_guide)
Click on the green <> Code button
Select “Download ZIP”

yml
text:
The file _quarto.yml determines the overall structure of the quarto website. It includes various segments.



Project: Determines what kind of project you create

This website focusses on creating a website project but you can also create books, manuscripts, and presentations with quarto

Website: General website and options and the structure of the website




One note is that indentation is vital in the file. Everything must be indented to to correct amount or creating the site will fail.
An example can be see in the following link containing the _quarto.yml file for this website.
The websites _quarto.yml on github

title: yml
text:
The type of project (i.e. is it a website, book, etc.)
For a normal quarto website you can have the following.

project:
  type: website







Tip



Note that the top line of a segment (i.e. project:) has no indentation. Then all lines in that segment have at least one level of indentations (e.g. type:website has one level).


You can also create:

Books
Manuscripts
Presentations

There are also other Project options than just type:. For example you can set the output director with output-dir:.

title: Callouts
text:
Callout out boxes are a nice way to signpost something. The below shows the callout boxes and the code that is included in the .qmd file to create them.
There are four types.

Note
Warning
Important
Caution

You can also include titles or make them collapsible.








Note



This is a note.


Code:

::: {.callout-note}
This is a note.
:::










Warning



Smoking leads to coughing


Code:

::: {.callout-warning}
Smoking leads to coughing
:::










Important



Remember to breath when stretching


Code:

::: {.callout-important}
Remember to breath when stretching
:::










Caution



Don’t get stuck in the circular loop of the next callout block


Code:

::: {.callout-caution}
Don't get stuck in the circular loops of the next callout blocks
:::




You can specify the title of a callout block.






NoteRead the note below



Read the title above


Code:

::: {.callout-note title="Read the note below"}
Read the title above
:::




You can make a callout block collapsible.
Set collapse="false" to make the block collapsible but not collapsed by default.






Warning





Hunger leads to eating




::: {.callout-warning collapse="false}
Hunger leads to eating
:::

Set collapse="TRUE" to make the collapsible block collapsed by default. Of course you can also add a title.






ImportantExpand this collapsible block





Collapse this expanded block




::: {.callout-important collapse="true" title="Expand this collapsible block"}
Collapse this expanded block
:::

title: Overview
text:
Authoring a website
Once you have created your various quarto files you can create your website’s html files with the following command in bash.

quarto preview







Note



Ensue you are in the main directory of your quarto project when running the above.


You can host your html files through various means. I use the free service GitHub pages.

text:
Creating quarto files
The various parts, sections, and pages of this website provide a quick guide and resources for creating a quarto website. These include:

Setup: Setting up quarto, VScode, and a quarto website project
qmd: Writing .qmd files with markdown
css: Setting the website theme, and the text font & colour

This shows the use of .scss files (Sass: Syntactically Awesome Style Sheets)

yml: Setting the format, structure, and other global options for the website
